content: Chlorhexidine gluconate (topical) is an antibacterial cleansing agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of gingivitis, periodontitis, and for use in skin cleansing procedures. Common adverse reactions include staining of teeth and other oral surfaces, calculus formation, alteration in taste perception, headache, and anaphylaxis. For surgical hand scrubbing, wet hands and forearms under running water for 30 seconds, clean fingernails with a nail stick or similar cleaner, and scrub for 5 minutes using approximately 8 mL of the product, with or without a wet brush, paying close attention to nails, cuticles, and the skin between fingers. Rinse under running water for 30 seconds and dry thoroughly. For healthcare personnel handwashing, wet hands with water, dispense about 5 mL of the product into cupped hands, wash vigorously for 15 seconds, rinse, and dry thoroughly. For preoperative skin preparation, apply the product liberally to the surgical site, swab for at least 2 minutes, and dry with a sterile towel. Repeat the procedure for an additional 2 minutes and dry with a sterile towel. For skin wound and general skin cleansing, thoroughly rinse the area to be cleaned with water, apply the minimum amount of product necessary to cover the skin or wound area, wash gently, and rinse again thoroughly. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of chlorhexidine gluconate (topical) in both adult and pediatric patients. Similarly, there is limited information on its contraindications, clinical trial experience, postmarketing experience, drug interactions, and monitoring requirements. Warnings include that this product is for external use only and must be kept out of reach of children. If swallowed, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised immediately. There is no FDA guidance on the use of chlorhexidine gluconate (topical) in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Additionally, there is no specific guidance for use in immunocompromised patients, specific genders, or racial populations. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of chlorhexidine gluconate (topical) are not well-documented in the drug label. Clinical studies and patient counseling information are also limited. The product should be stored at 20-25°C (68-77°F) and excessive heat above 40°C (104°F) should be avoided. There is no established interaction between alcohol and chlorhexidine gluconate (topical), but patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication.
